rules.scope_resolution: Resolvers are identifiers for reviewed implementations, not arbitrary commands. Resolve sorted exact paths and selectors; no wildcard is a write target. Overlapping preserve/exclude scopes dominate mutation candidates.
rules.adoption: When no valid bound receipt exists, construct a read-only candidate inventory from exact known source versions and current files. Explicitly reviewed exact-path/selector adoption is required before replacement; matching names or hashes alone do not establish authority. Unknown entries remain preserved.
rules.obsolete: Removal requires exact prior ownership plus current source absence and selected client applicability. Shared-section retirement restores its recorded original value only after current ownership is established; unknown or conflicting ownership blocks.
rules.receipt_binding: Validate schema, catalog/version, source and target identities, binding hash, selected clients, path/selector uniqueness and category scope. A local receipt is evidence, not authentication or human approval.
rules.plan_basis: Canonical UTF-8 JSON with sorted keys and stable array order hashes source/target/catalog/client selection/prior receipt hash/resolved mutations before output ownership receipt and execution events. Store this digest as plan_basis_sha256 in the receipt; the final plan token can bind the receipt after-hash without self-reference.
rules.clock: Ownership payload has no timestamps. Review-ledger execution intent binds old ledger hash, fixed event fields and plan binding; execution time and realized after-hash are recorded after apply. A no-op emits no event.
rules.verification: Whole files use exact bytes; marked blocks, TOML keys and JSON entries use ownership-aware checks plus preserved-remainder checks. Existing whole-file Codex verifier is insufficient.
rules.content_hashes: Whole-file and marked-block installed_sha256 bind exact bytes (UTF-8 for block text). TOML key and JSON entry installed_sha256 bind canonical UTF-8 JSON of their typed value: sorted object keys, compact separators, ensure_ascii=False, no trailing newline, and no NaN/Infinity. original.sha256 uses the same representation as that entry; absent originals omit both value and hash.
rules.selector_identity: Receipt entries are unique by normalized path plus ownership kind and selector. Markers must be unique and non-overlapping. TOML key paths are arrays of exact literal keys. A JSON entry selector names one exact array pointer and matches one canonical entry hash; zero or multiple matches are conflicts unless an explicitly reviewed adoption resolves them.
rules.receipt_entry_scope: Receipt payload entries are only replaceable source or integration units (whole_file, marked_block, toml_key, json_entry). Runtime state, preserved documents, generated receipts, execution journals and backups never become deletion-authorized payload entries. Validate every entry against its entity kind, resolver destination scope and selected client.
rules.idempotence: Before deriving a successor basis or ownership receipt, compare desired payload, source/catalog/generator identities, selected clients and exact ownership entries with the verified installed state, excluding transaction provenance plan_basis_sha256. If no material delta or owned-file repair exists, reuse existing receipt bytes and emit no writes or events. Never make the prior receipt hash alone cause a successor receipt.

entities.notes: Resolve exact package-files.json members under asdg/. Validate both the source manifest and prior ownership evidence. Extra files are not owned by directory membership.
Only exact files emitted from canonical templates/.agents/skills; no directory wildcard deletion.
Only exact canonical templates/.codex/agents files, including the coordinator.
Render every selected canonical skill and remove only exact retired adapter files proven owned by prior inventory.
Resolve exact MOD_FILES for each validated canonical mod; companions and tests stay in asdg/.
Recognized legacy markers require explicit resolver mapping; duplicated, missing or ambiguous boundaries block replacement.
Destination is root CLAUDE.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md. Existing user-written imports remain user-owned; parent instruction files are read-only evidence.
Preserve unrelated ignore rules byte-for-byte.

Writer and verifier must both inspect the owned key. Preserve unrelated keys and formatting. A shared feature switch is not exclusive ASDG ownership or hook trust; existing user choice requires explicit adoption.
Own exact identified ASDG hook entries, not parent arrays or unrelated hooks. Validate selector uniqueness; compare entries semantically and preserve unrelated content.
Retain selected clients; do not silently add or remove integrations.
Preserve existing upstream records. Existing schema permits promote/upgrade only; push-replace requires explicit compatible record semantics, never an unrecognized operation value.
Attribute only matching committed package bytes; remove a stale record for unattributed source.
Receipt governed by the adjacent schema. No schema-valid receipt alone authenticates historical ownership. Never inventory this receipt as a replaceable payload entry.
The deterministic plan binds the old ledger hash and typed event intent. recorded_at and realized ledger after-hash belong to the execution envelope; a no-op adds no events.
Validate schema compatibility without mutating identity, lifecycle or sprint state; migrations require separate scope.
Preserve all saved team definitions and related client records.
Despite the cache directory name these receipts establish prior team writes and must not be cleared.
Preserve every other cache entry too; push replacement is not cache cleanup.
Shared among linked worktrees. Never overwrite active claims or acquire/delete the team lock as the replacement lock. Runtime compatibility/liveness is reported separately.
Contains full Git worktrees and application work. Do not recurse into them as integration files or independently update them without explicit target selection.
ASDG team setup can add .claude/worktrees/ to info/exclude; replacement preserves all Git metadata, refs and worktree registrations.
Preserve the default identity and any explicitly configured alternate identity. Never inspect or reset arbitrary host state as a side effect.
All client artifacts are preserved, including generated stage READMEs; missing-scaffold creation belongs to explicit initialization.
Retain existing data. New replacement backups use a distinct transaction namespace and record exact original bytes/modes; no purge.
OpenSpec skills and commands remain externally owned; resolver lists them read-only and cannot authorize ASDG replacement.
Chat membership, active sessions, skill discovery, terminals and trust are native runtime objects; file checks do not prove them ready.
